# Vendored str0m-rust-crypto 0.7.0

`str0m-rust-crypto/` is crates.io **str0m-rust-crypto 0.7.0** (MIT OR Apache-2.0,
Martin Algesten, <https://github.com/algesten/str0m>, upstream commit
`5f2183ce7c67117cd1960dfeb11bed11fc188b66`, path `crypto/rust-crypto`),
with the changes in `str0m-rust-crypto.patch` (a unified diff against the pristine crate).
The pristine `.crate` SHA-256 is
`298554811ee24adbfee0bf8628c2e220989543c83c55c3869437dc1f3a43e340`.
`rs-net/Cargo.toml` points `[patch.crates-io]` here. Registry dependencies remain pinned
by `rs-net/Cargo.lock`. `Cargo.lock`, `Cargo.toml.orig`, and `.cargo_vcs_info.json`
were omitted. The upstream MIT license text, absent from this crate archive, is
copied from the cached str0m 0.25.0 release from the same upstream commit.

The patch drops dimpl's `rcgen` feature and makes `generate_certificate()` return
`None`. The embedding application always supplies a persistent ECDSA P-256
certificate generated by its existing ring-backed rcgen. This avoids dimpl's
certificate generator enabling rcgen's default aws-lc backend and linking a C
crypto library into the RustCrypto backend. DTLS, STUN, and SRTP are unchanged.

To refresh, unpack the pristine crate, apply the patch, retain the license, and
run rs-net's release tests with and without `--features rtc`. Check that
`cargo tree --offline -i aws-lc-sys --features rtc --target all` and the equivalent
command for `openssl-sys` find no matching package.
